title: Pan-Seared Seabass with Lemon Butter Beurre Blanc
description: Pan-Seared Seabass with Lemon Butter Beurre Blanc is a refined continental seafood dish featuring perfectly crisp skin, tender flaky flesh, and a silky French beurre blanc enriched with fresh lemon and herbs. Elegant accompaniments and precise technique make it a signature fine-dining restaurant classic.

ingredients.title: For the Seabass
items: 2 seabass fillets, skin on (about 6 oz / 170 g each), pin bones removed
Maldon sea salt (or fine sea salt), to taste
2 tbsp clarified butter or light olive oil

ingredients.title: For the Lemon Butter Beurre Blanc
items: ½ cup dry white wine (Sauvignon Blanc or Chardonnay)
Juice of ½ a lemon (reserve the other half for garnish)
1 tbsp heavy cream (optional, for extra silkiness)

ingredients.title: For Garnish & Accompaniments
items: Seasonal vegetables (e.g., butter-glazed asparagus or baby carrots)
Potato purée or a cauliflower velouté

instruction.title: 1. Prepare the Seabass
steps: Pat fillets dry thoroughly; moisture prevents crisp skin.
Season both sides lightly with sea salt and white pepper.

instruction.title: 2. Pan-Sear the Seabass
steps: Heat clarified butter in a heavy-bottom skillet (preferably stainless steel) over medium-high heat.
Place seabass skin-side down; gently press with a fish spatula for 15 seconds to prevent curling.
Cook undisturbed for 4–5 minutes until the skin is golden and crisp.
Flip carefully and cook the flesh side for 1–2 minutes until just opaque and tender.
Remove from the pan and rest on a warm plate.

instruction.title: 3. Prepare the Lemon Butter Beurre Blanc
steps: In a small saucepan, combine minced shallot, white wine, and vinegar.
Reduce over medium heat until only 2–3 tbsp of liquid remain (a syrupy consistency).
Add lemon juice, then whisk in cold butter cubes gradually over low heat to form a smooth, glossy sauce.
Optional: Stir in a splash of cream for added stability.
Strain sauce through a fine sieve for elegance, then finish with parsley and chives.

instruction.title: 4. Plating & Garnish
steps: Spoon a pool of beurre blanc onto each warm plate.
Place the seabass fillet skin-side up (to showcase crispness).
Arrange glazed vegetables and a quenelle of potato purée (or cauliflower velouté) alongside.
Garnish with microgreens, a curl of lemon zest, and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Wine pairing: Sauvignon Blanc (citrusy, crisp) or lightly oaked Chardonnay.

chefTips: Variation: For more depth, infuse the beurre blanc with a touch of saffron or a sprig of tarragon.
Texture balance: Crisp skin, velvety sauce, and creamy purée create contrast.
